terms.gloss: in effect, in practice (as opposed to name or words)
terms.grammar: the ablative of rēs, set against verbō or nōmine
evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 123: tametsī verbō nōn audeat, tamen rē ipsā dē maleficiō suō cōnfitērī (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Ac. 2.15: nōminibus differentēs, rē congruentēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Latin says “in effect” by contrast: verbō … rē, in word … in fact; nōmine … rē, in name … in effect (Lewis & Short, s.v. rēs). With vērā it is “actually, in truth” (see actually); for “virtually, all but” see almost.

phrases.latin: eum, tametsī verbō nōn audeat, tamen rē ipsā dē maleficiō suō cōnfitērī
phrases.english: that though he would not dare to say so, he is in effect confessing his crime

phrases.latin: Peripatēticōs et Acadēmicōs nōminibus differentēs, rē congruentēs
phrases.english: the Peripatetics and the Academics, different in name, in effect agreeing

sources: Lewis & Short: res
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
